title: His therapists died; trying the gag reflex himself
summary: Gil tells how his therapist and then the therapist's brother died, and how he still tries the technique.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Over how long a period of time?
Over how long a period of time?

I just took it for a few months and then I stopped and then went back again for a few more months. Then the therapist that was treating me died. I walked in his office one day and there was a notice on the door saying he had died. You know, it was like you're suddenly cut off and I went home and hollered and screamed and cried because it was such a, well the shock of it, but when somebody close to you dies you cry for the you that goes with them.

That's what you cry for. The combination of you and that person that is dead forever. Some part of you always goes with them, someone you know and love dearly who dies. And you cry for that part of yourself.
Then I stopped taking that treatment for a while. And then I went to the same man's brother out in Long Island a few times. Anyhow, it wasn't too long after that he died too.
Well it's okay. I got quite a bit of what I wanted out of it but if I had the luxury of knowing somebody like that and could go occasionally you know to help me, I'd go.

These men had worked with radiation
........(VOICE FADES OUT).
Are you able to adapt any part of it, you know, yourself? In other words, do you know how to bring about this kind of relief right now?

Now it's hard for me to do that. I try to do that sometimes. Now I can't get it passed the gag. It's hard for me to get the thing to go like ....t h a t..... And throw that all the way out. Because when that thing goes out you know you've let something go. You can tell even though you can't see it. It's the energy in you that's been stuck there and you know that you've let something out. It's fantastic.
Then when you've let that out, then your mind is clearer?
If that's your problem, you've found a way of dealing with it?

All of a sudden this feeling that's been stopping you. Like you've been so mad and sulking and wanting to get revenge and going through all that, that's been wasting your time, you know. Oh yes, a great thing.
